notice: Simulated MVP Result — Not actual airport performance. Scenario definitions below describe illustrative causal chains calibrated against cited public incident reports; they are design inputs for the synthetic event generator, not a record of SKY ICT or any named airline's internal operations.

provenance_tiers.TIER_A_OFFICIAL: Civil aviation authority, airport operator, national weather/disaster agency, ICAO/IATA/WHO official statements. Used for REAL_PUBLIC facts: that an event occurred, when, and its officially reported scale.
provenance_tiers.TIER_B_INDUSTRY: Industry bodies (SITA, ACI, Eurocontrol) and benchmark reports. Used for BENCHMARK distributions (e.g. baggage mishandling cost per bag), not for airport-specific telemetry.
provenance_tiers.TIER_C_NEWS: High-quality wire/press reporting (Reuters, AP, Thai PBS). Used for incident timeline and reported impact magnitude, never as sole ground truth.
provenance_tiers.TIER_D_ASSUMPTION: No external source; team-set operating parameter (staff counts, capacities, thresholds) explicitly tagged ASSUMPTION and never presented as a real company's figures.

scenarios.name: flood_baggage_compound
scenarios.hero_scenario_note: Promoted to the primary/default demo scenario on 2026-10-07 after narrowing the One TrustX pitch to 'Baggage Disruption Recovery' as the hero use case. See docs/decisions/2026-10-07-baggage-disruption-scope-narrowing.md.
scenarios.summary: Heavy rain and urban flooding in Bangkok reduce ground-handling staff availability, which backs up baggage processing and cascades into flight delay and transfer risk.

real_public_context.fact: CAAT notice on heavy rain and flooding affecting access to Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang
AOT tracking page for Thai Airways passenger baggage stranded at Suvarnabhumi, 26-29 Sep 2026
Thai Airways operational update: cancellations/rescheduling 29 Sep - 3 Oct 2026
Reported ~5,000 bags stranded at one point during the event (29 Sep 2026)
Follow-up reporting: cause cited as a mix of ground-handling staff shortage (flood commute impact) and baggage-cart/tug availability, producing cascading effects across baggage and flight operations

benchmark_context.source: Industry benchmark cited in SKY deck / SITA Baggage IT Insights
benchmark_context.caveat: Original SKY deck figure (page 1: $60.3B/year, ~$260/bag). Does not reconcile cleanly with SITA's own global totals below; treat as deck-sourced, not independently re-derived.

benchmark_context.metric: share of mishandling from transfer bags
benchmark_context.source: Industry benchmark cited in SKY deck

benchmark_context.metric: global mishandled bags, 2025 (most recent, use this one)
benchmark_context.note: Never say these bags were 'lost' — SITA's figure is mishandled (delayed/damaged/misrouted), and most are recovered.

assumption_parameters.note: Illustrative operating parameters for the synthetic model. Not a disclosed staffing or capacity figure of any named airline, ground handler, or airport operator.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: Whether the shared state correctly flags CAPACITY_DEGRADED from a late/partial staffing update, and whether the recommendation changes once the update arrives versus staying stale.

scenarios.name: geopolitical_airspace_closure
scenarios.summary: A regional airspace closure or conflict-zone advisory forces route and schedule replanning with short notice.

real_public_context.fact: ICAO maintains conflict zone risk information used by states and operators for route-planning advisories

assumption_parameters.note: Illustrative planning parameters; not a real route-closure event for BKK.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: Whether conflicting NOTAM/advisory sources are reconciled to one shared routing-risk state before schedule replanning begins.

scenarios.name: terminal_utility_fire
scenarios.summary: A localized fire or utility failure in a terminal zone forces partial evacuation and takes gates/systems offline.

assumption_parameters.note: Hypothetical drill-style scenario; no real incident referenced.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: Whether the system keeps a coherent affected-gate list when sensor/manual reports duplicate or go silent mid-incident.

scenarios.name: health_screening_disruption
scenarios.summary: An elevated health-screening requirement (communicable disease response) adds immigration/security dwell time industry-wide.

real_public_context.fact: WHO publishes disease outbreak and response data used for public-health advisories affecting travel

assumption_parameters.note: Illustrative dwell-time addition; not a specific disease's measured effect at BKK.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: Whether queue-risk forecasts update promptly when a health-advisory parameter change is published.

scenarios.name: bhs_and_trust_pipeline_outage
scenarios.summary: The baggage handling system (BHS) and/or One TrustX's own ingest pipeline degrades, producing an operational failure AND a data failure at the same time — this is the scenario that stress-tests our own system, not just the airport.

assumption_parameters.note: This is the explicit 'operational failure vs data failure' test case: ground truth is BHS_DOWN, but at least one source stays stale and reports NORMAL. Pass condition is that the trusted common state matches ground truth, not the stale source.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: This is the core resilience test: can One TrustX itself keep producing a correct shared state when its own inputs are degraded, not just when the airport is degraded.

scenarios.name: terminal_power_disruption
scenarios.summary: Partial terminal power loss degrades jet bridges, conveyor systems and check-in kiosks simultaneously.

assumption_parameters.note: Illustrative infrastructure-dependency scenario per the PDF's Next-Forward Energy & Utilities dependency.

scenarios.trust_x_test_focus: Whether systems correctly distinguish full outage from partial/degraded capacity instead of flattening both to one status.
